name: What is the difference between a tank and tankless water heater?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tank and tankless water heater?

acceptedAnswer.text: A traditional tank water heater stores and continuously heats a set amount of water, ready for use. A tankless water heater, also known as an on-demand water heater, heats water directly as it flows through the unit when you turn on a hot water tap. Tankless units are generally more energy-efficient and provide an endless supply of hot water, but they typically have a higher upfront installation cost. Tank heaters are less expensive initially but use more energy over time. The choice depends on your household's hot water needs and budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tank heaters store and pre-heat water, while tankless heaters heat water on demand. Tankless are more energy-efficient but have higher initial costs.
